entries.dictionary: デジタル大辞泉; 普及版 字通
entries.heading: いん【允】［漢字項目］; 允人名用漢字4画
entries.evidence: Daijisen explicitly labels the character name-use, gives イン with kun ゆるす/じょう, distinguishes recognizing/permitting from まことに, and lists 允可/允許/承允 versus 允文允武. Jitsu gives four strokes, イン and truth/fit/permit glosses; its historical dictionary section includes マコトニ.
entries.decision: Keep all four exact frozen readings and their order. Propose only イン for quiz recognition through 允可. Preserve まこと.に as reference-only classical/adverbial lookup information and ゆるす as a permission gloss, not an invented ordinary spelling 允す. Names/nanori are not transported into quizzes.
entries.limits: Neither the spelling list nor missing JMdict priority flags measure frequency. Jitsu's historical forms and gaiji are images not inspected; no historical derivation or phonetic claim is adopted. Use a labelled modern-shape mnemonic with canonical radical 儿10, not the alternative Nelson radical 厶28.

entries.dictionary: デジタル大辞泉; 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 普及版 字通
entries.heading: いん‐か【×允可】; いん‐か【允可】
entries.evidence: Daijisen gives noun/suru permission and directly compares 許可/允許. Nikkoku explicitly explains that 允 itself means permit and attests the permission-obtaining construction in an1868 governmental text. Jitsu cross-refers to 允許. The full frozen JMdict1627840 family independently gives the exact unrestricted 允可いんか pair, noun/transitive-suru and permission/assent/compliance glosses.
entries.decision: Select 允可いんか as the single necessary new support for イン, for recognition of permission/assent in formal or older writing rather than a default casual request. Raw 允イン/可カ, the exact unrestricted word and explicit public explanation jointly support allocation. A future article may teach 允可を得る with its kana, gloss and historical-context qualification. Compare ordinary 許可 without asserting an absolute legal, imperial-only or temporal boundary.
entries.limits: The1868 attestation establishes an actual historical construction, not measured present-day frequency, a claim of total obsolescence or unrestricted modern substitution. The × marker is not itself a rare-pronunciation label. Any new complete Japanese examples still require independent review.

entries.dictionary: デジタル大辞泉; 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 普及版 字通
entries.heading: いん‐きょ【×允許】; いん‐きょ【允許】
entries.evidence: Daijisen gives noun/suru permission. Nikkoku explicitly states that 允 also means permit, relates permission/license/sanction and supplies historical attestations. Jitsu gives permission/consent.
entries.decision: Retain this exact whole-word alternative in evidence; it does not require another article for the already supported sole on-reading. Do not equate every permission noun with forgiveness, driving credentials or all administrative procedures.
entries.limits: Source examples include old forms and gaiji. The returned7000-character page includes all three relevant dictionary entries but not the complete footer; no new frequency or historical-grammar course is claimed.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
entries.heading: うた‐の‐じょう【雅楽允】
entries.evidence: The exact headword names the third class of officials in the historical 雅楽寮 and distinguishes 大允/少允. Its attestation is from the tenth-century 宇津保物語. Frozen JMdict2857093 independently labels the term historical and gives うたのじょう.
entries.decision: Explain じょう as an attested historical office-title reading, with 雅楽允うたのじょう as a plain-text example. Do not label it nonexistent, an arbitrary personal-name reading or an everyday modern job title. Exclude it from this practical quiz subset; no extra specialist support article is necessary.
entries.limits: The JMdict English rendering 'second assistant court musician' is retained raw, not silently equated with the Japanese ordinal 第三 or a claim that the official performed music. Teach a neutral historical official-title gloss; no independent ritsuryo administrative-history audit is claimed.
